DIAGNOSIS READY: Congestive Heart Failure secondary to an Atrial Septal Defect (ASD).

The echocardiogram confirms a left-to-right shunt, which explains the rapid breathing (tachypnea) and leg swelling (peripheral edema) due to blood backing up into the lungs and systemic circulation. The enlarged liver (hepatomegaly) is a classic sign of right-sided heart failure in this context.
